ko.title: 할부로 사는 식료품: 미국 18조 8천억 달러 부채 더미 속의 K자형 양극화

segments.src: American household debt has reached a record of roughly **$18.8 trillion**, with about **$1.25 trillion** of that sitting on credit cards.
segments.tr: 미국의 가계 부채는 약 **18조 8천억 달러**라는 기록적인 수치에 도달했으며, 그중 약 **1조 2500억 달러**가 신용카드에 묶여 있습니다.

segments.src: Those are big, round, headline-friendly numbers — and, taken alone, they explain almost nothing.
segments.tr: 이러한 수치들은 크고 둥글며 언론에 인용하기 좋지만, 이것만으로는 거의 아무것도 설명하지 못합니다.

segments.src: The more revealing detail is buried underneath.
segments.tr: 더욱 시사하는 바가 큰 세부 사항은 그 이면에 파묻혀 있습니다.

segments.src: Aggregate balances have largely flattened out.
segments.tr: 전체 잔액은 대체로 정체되었습니다.

segments.src: Yet the share of card balances slipping into serious delinquency has stayed stubbornly close to levels the U.S.
segments.tr: 그럼에도 불구하고 심각한 연체 상태로 빠져드는 카드 잔액의 비중은 미국이 2008년 금융위기 직후 몇 년 동안

segments.src: last saw in the years immediately following the 2008 financial crisis.
segments.tr: 마지막으로 목격했던 수준에 고집스럽게 머물러 있습니다.

segments.src: Those two facts do not fit together comfortably.
segments.tr: 이 두 가지 사실은 편안하게 어우러지지 않습니다.

segments.src: Debt that is no longer growing quickly should not, in theory, be going bad at a rate reminiscent of a credit downturn.
segments.tr: 이론상으로 빠르게 증가하지 않는 부채는 신용 침체를 연상시키는 비율로 부실화되어서는 안 됩니다.

segments.src: The explanation is that the national average is now describing two very different populations at once.
segments.tr: 이에 대한 설명은 국가 평균이 이제 두 가지 매우 다른 인구 집단을 동시에 묘사하고 있다는 점입니다.

segments.src: ## The number that stopped moving, and the number that didn't
segments.tr: ## 움직임을 멈춘 숫자와 멈추지 않은 숫자

segments.src: Quarterly household-debt data compiled by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York from a nationally representative sample of consumer credit reports gives the clearest public view of this.
segments.tr: 소비자 신용 보고서의 전국 대표 표본을 바탕으로 뉴욕 연방준비은행이 집계한 분기별 가계 부채 데이터는 이에 대한 가장 명확한 공공의 시야를 제공합니다.

segments.src: It tracks mortgages, auto loans, student loans, and credit cards — and, critically, it tracks *flows*: how much debt moved from current into 30-day, 90-day, and 120-day-plus delinquency each quarter.
segments.tr: 이 데이터는 주택담보대출, 자동차 대출, 학자금 대출, 신용카드를 추적하며, 특히 *흐름(flows)*을 추적합니다. 즉, 매분기 얼마나 많은 부채가 정상 상태에서 30일, 90일, 120일 이상 연체 상태로 넘어갔는지를 보여줍니다.

segments.src: Aggregate growth has cooled.
segments.tr: 전체적인 성장은 둔화되었습니다.

segments.src: Mortgage origination remains constrained by high rates and thin inventory.
segments.tr: 주택담보대출 실행은 높은 금리와 부족한 매물로 인해 계속 제한을 받고 있습니다.

segments.src: Card balances, which climbed steeply through the post-pandemic period, have settled into a slower rhythm.
segments.tr: 팬데믹 이후 급격히 증가했던 카드 잔액은 더 느린 리듬으로 안정되었습니다.

segments.src: On a chart of total balances, the last several quarters look almost calm.
segments.tr: 총 잔액 차트에서 지난 몇 분기는 거의 평온해 보입니다.

segments.src: The transition rates do not look calm.
segments.tr: 전환율은 평온해 보이지 않습니다.

segments.src: The share of credit card balances moving into serious delinquency has hovered near post-2008 highs rather than normalizing back toward the mid-2010s baseline.
segments.tr: 심각한 연체로 진입하는 신용카드 잔액의 비중은 2010년대 중반의 기준선으로 정규화되는 대신 2008년 이후 최고점 근처를 맴돌고 있습니다.

segments.src: Auto loans show a related pattern, with subprime borrowers driving most of the deterioration.
segments.tr: 자동차 대출도 이와 유사한 패턴을 보이며, 서브프라임 차주들이 악화의 대부분을 주도하고 있습니다.

segments.src: When balances flatten but delinquency transitions stay elevated, it usually means the composition of borrowing has shifted.
segments.tr: 잔액은 정체되는데 연체 전환율이 높은 상태를 유지한다면, 이는 대출의 구성이 바뀌었음을 의미합니다.

segments.src: Fewer people are adding debt — but the people still adding it are, on average, less able to service it.
segments.tr: 부채를 추가하는 사람은 줄어들었지만, 여전히 부채를 추가하는 사람들은 평균적으로 이를 상환할 능력이 떨어집니다.

segments.src: ## What "K-shaped" actually means here
segments.tr: ## 여기서 'K자형'이 실제로 의미하는 것

segments.src: The letter is a shorthand for divergence: one group's trajectory bending upward while another's bends down, from the same starting point.
segments.tr: 이 알파벳은 괴리를 나타내는 약칭입니다. 동일한 출발점에서 한 그룹의 궤도는 위로 꺾이고 다른 그룹의 궤도는 아래로 꺾이는 현상입니다.

segments.src: **The upper stroke.** Borrowers with prime and super-prime credit scores have been paying down revolving balances.
segments.tr: **상단 줄기.** 우량(prime) 및 최우량(super-prime) 신용 점수를 가진 차주들은 회전식 잔액을 갚아나고 있습니다.

segments.src: Many locked in mortgages at 3% or lower before 2022 and are effectively insulated from the rate cycle.
segments.tr: 많은 이들이 2022년 이전에 3% 이하로 주택담보대출을 고정하여 금리 주기로부터 사실상 보호받고 있습니다.

segments.src: Their financial assets have appreciated.
segments.tr: 그들의 금융 자산은 가치가 올랐습니다.

segments.src: For this group, higher interest rates have been closer to a feature than a bug — money-market yields and short-duration Treasuries have paid them to hold cash.
segments.tr: 이 그룹에게는 높은 이자율이 단점보다는 장점에 가까웠습니다. 머니마켓 수익률과 단기 국채가 현금을 보유하는 대가로 이자를 지불해주었기 때문입니다.

segments.src: They are deleveraging by choice, not necessity.
segments.tr: 이들은 필수가 아닌 선택에 의해 레버리지를 축소하고 있습니다.

segments.src: **The lower stroke.** Borrowers in the non-prime tiers are carrying more revolving debt at rates that, for many cards, sit above 20% APR.
segments.tr: **하단 줄기.** 비우량(non-prime) 계층의 차주들은 많은 카드에서 20% APR(연이율)을 웃도는 금리로 더 많은 회전식 부채를 떠안고 있습니다.

segments.src: They are far more likely to rent, which means the housing-cost lock-in that protected homeowners never applied to them.
segments.tr: 이들은 임차인일 확률이 훨씬 높으며, 이는 주택 소유자들을 보호해주었던 주거비 고정 혜택이 이들에게는 전혀 적용되지 않았음을 의미합니다.

segments.src: They have absorbed several years of cumulative price increases in groceries, insurance, utilities, and childcare on wages that, for many, rose but not by enough to close the gap.
segments.tr: 이들은 식료품, 보험, 공공요금, 보육료에서 수년간 누적된 물가 인상을 흡수해왔으나, 많은 이들의 임금은 그 격차를 메울 만큼 오르지 않았습니다.

segments.src: Average them together and you get "household balance sheets are broadly healthy."
segments.tr: 이들을 평균내면 "가계 대차대조표가 전반적으로 건전하다"는 결론이 나옵니다.

segments.src: That statement is true of the aggregate and misleading about the distribution — which is precisely the problem with reading a $18.8 trillion figure as a single signal.
segments.tr: 그 진술은 전체 집계에는 맞지만 분포에 대해서는 오해를 불러일으키며, 이것이 바로 18조 8천억 달러라는 수치를 단일 신호로 읽을 때 발생하는 문제점입니다.

segments.src: ## The part that changes the character of the debt
segments.tr: ## 부채의 성격을 바꾸는 부분

segments.src: Here is the shift that matters most, and it is qualitative rather than numerical.
segments.tr: 여기서 가장 중요한 변화가 있으며, 이는 수치적인 것보다는 질적인 변화입니다.

segments.src: Historically, revolving credit expanded fastest around discretionary consumption — electronics, travel, furniture, holiday spending.
segments.tr: 역사적으로 회전 신용은 재량적 소비(전자기기, 여행, 가구, 휴가 지출)를 중심으로 가장 빠르게 확대되었습니다.

segments.src: Card debt was, broadly, a way to pull forward purchases that could otherwise have waited.
segments.tr: 카드 부채는 대체로 나중에 구매할 수 있었던 소비를 앞당겨 실행하는 수단이었습니다.

segments.src: A growing share of new non-prime borrowing now goes toward things that cannot wait.
segments.tr: 현재 비우량 신용대출 신규 차입의 점점 더 많은 부분이 미룰 수 없는 것들에 쓰이고 있습니다.

segments.src: Surveys from the Federal Reserve, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, and multiple consumer-finance researchers have documented households using credit cards and short-term installment products for groceries, rent, utility bills, insurance premiums, and medical costs.
segments.tr: 연방준비제도, 소비자금융보호국, 그리고 여러 소비자 금융 연구원들의 조사에 따르면 가계가 식료품, 월세, 공공요금, 보험료, 의료비를 위해 신용카드와 단기 할부 상품을 사용하고 있음이 기록되어 있습니다.

segments.src: Buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) is the clearest illustration.
segments.tr: 선구매 후결제(BNPL)는 이를 가장 명확하게 보여주는 예입니다.

segments.src: The product was built for mid-ticket discretionary retail — a jacket, a pair of headphones, a mattress.
segments.tr: 이 상품은 중저가 재량형 소매 쇼핑(재킷, 헤드폰, 매트리스)을 위해 만들어졌습니다.

segments.src: Its fastest-growing use cases increasingly include supermarket orders, food delivery, and everyday essentials split into four payments over six weeks.
segments.tr: 하지만 가장 빠르게 성장하는 사용처는 점점 슈퍼마켓 주문, 음식 배달, 그리고 6주 동안 4회로 나누어 지불하는 일상 필수품으로 확대되고 있습니다.

segments.src: Debt used to smooth a shortfall behaves differently from debt used to accelerate a purchase.
segments.tr: 부족한 자금을 메우기 위해 사용된 부채는 구매를 앞당기기 위해 사용된 부채와 다르게 움직입니다.

segments.src: A television bought on credit is a one-time obligation.
segments.tr: 신용으로 구매한 텔레비전은 일회성 채무입니다.

segments.src: Groceries bought on credit recur every week, which means the balance does not naturally retire itself — it compounds against a bill that arrives again in seven days.
segments.tr: 신용으로 구매한 식료품은 매주 반복되므로 잔액이 자연스럽게 해소되지 않으며, 7일마다 다시 돌아오는 청구서와 맞물려 복리로 불어납니다.

segments.src: That is why the delinquency-transition series can stay elevated even as total balances plateau: the borrowing has become less about wants and more about the gap between a paycheck and a fixed monthly cost floor.
segments.tr: 이것이 바로 전체 잔액이 정체되는 동안에도 연체 전환율 시리즈가 높은 수준을 유지할 수 있는 이유입니다. 대출이 원해서 하는 소비보다는 월급과 고정된 월 생활비 바닥 사이의 격차에 관한 것이 되었기 때문입니다.

segments.src: ## The measurement blind spot
segments.tr: ## 측정의 사각지대

segments.src: There is an important caveat that responsible readings of this data should include: **BNPL is only partially visible.**
segments.tr: 이 데이터를 책임감 있게 해석하려면 반드시 포함해야 할 중요한 단서가 있습니다. **BNPL은 부분적으로만 가시화되어 있습니다.**

segments.src: Most BNPL "pay-in-four" plans have historically not been furnished to the traditional credit bureaus in the same consistent way as cards and installment loans.
segments.tr: 대부분의 BNPL '4회 분할 납부' 플랜은 역사적으로 카드나 할부 대출과 같은 일관된 방식으로 전통적인 신용평가기관에 제공되지 않았습니다.

segments.src: Reporting practices have been changing, and major bureaus and lenders have moved toward incorporating this data — but the transition is uneven and recent.
segments.tr: 보고 관행이 변화하고 있으며 주요 평가기관과 대출기관들이 이 데이터를 통합하는 방향으로 움직이고 있지만, 전환 과정은 고르지 않고 최근의 일입니다.

segments.src: The practical consequence is that the official household-debt total almost certainly understates total consumer obligations, and that a household can appear less leveraged in bureau data than it actually is.
segments.tr: 실질적인 결과는 공식 가계 부채 총액이 전체 소비자 채무를 거의 확실하게 과소평가하고 있으며, 가계가 실제보다 신용평가사 데이터상에서 레버리지가 낮은 것처럼 보일 수 있다는 점입니다.

segments.src: It also creates "loan stacking" risk, where a borrower holds several concurrent plans from different providers, none of which can see the others.
segments.tr: 또한 이는 차주가 서로의 존재를 볼 수 없는 여러 제공업체의 동시 플랜을 여러 개 보유하는 '대출 중첩(loan stacking)' 위험을 발생시킵니다.

segments.src: This does not invalidate the $18.8 trillion figure.
segments.tr: 그렇다고 해서 18조 8천억 달러라는 수치가 무효화되는 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: It means the figure should be read as a floor for one category of borrowing, not a ceiling.
segments.tr: 이는 이 수치가 대출 한계선이 아니라 한 가지 차입 범주에 대한 하한선으로 읽혀야 함을 의미합니다.

segments.src: ## Why aggregate stability can persist for a long time
segments.tr: ## 총체적 안정성이 장기간 지속될 수 있는 이유

segments.src: It would be a mistake to read elevated card delinquencies as a forecast of systemic stress.
segments.tr: 상승한 카드 연체율을 체계적 스트레스의 예측으로 읽는 것은 오판일 것입니다.

segments.src: Several structural factors argue against a direct 2008 analogy:
segments.tr: 몇 가지 구조적 요인들이 2008년과의 직접적인 비유에 반대합니다:

segments.src: - **Mortgage debt, the dominant component, is qualitatively different this cycle.** Post-crisis underwriting standards, the near-absence of the 2000s-era exotic products, and the enormous stock of fixed-rate loans originated below 4% make the largest slice of household debt unusually resilient.
segments.tr: - **지배적인 구성 요소인 주택담보대출 부채는 이번 주기에 질적으로 다릅니다.** 위기 이후의 언더라이팅 기준, 2000년대식 이색 상품의 거의 부재, 그리고 4% 미만으로 실행된 엄청난 규모의 고정금리 대출 재고 덕분에 가계 부채의 가장 큰 파편이 유례없이 회복력을 갖추고 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Credit card debt is a small share of the total.** At roughly $1.25 trillion against $18.8 trillion, cards represent under 7% of household liabilities. Severe stress in that segment is painful for the households involved and manageable for the financial system.
segments.tr: - **신용카드 부채는 전체에서 차지하는 비중이 작습니다.** 18조 8천억 달러 대비 약 1조 2500억 달러로, 카드는 가계 부채의 7% 미만을 차지합니다. 해당 부문의 심각한 스트레스는 관련 가계에는 고통스럽지만 금융 시스템에는 관리 가능한 수준입니다.

segments.src: - **Lenders have already adjusted.** Card issuers have tightened approval criteria, trimmed credit lines, and provisioned against losses over multiple quarters. The deterioration has not been a surprise to the institutions holding the exposure.
segments.tr: - **대출기관들은 이미 조정을 마쳤습니다.** 카드 발행사들은 승인 기준을 강화하고, 신용 한도를 축소하며, 여러 분기에 걸쳐 손실에 대비한 충당금을 적립했습니다. 이러한 악화는 익스포저를 보유한 기관들에게 놀랄 일도 아니었습니다.

segments.src: The realistic reading is not "crisis pending."
segments.tr: 현실적인 해석은 "위기 임박"이 아닙니다.

segments.src: It is that a meaningful and growing minority of households are running a persistent monthly deficit and financing it with the most expensive credit available to them — while the aggregate statistics, dominated by wealthier balance sheets, register that as stability.
segments.tr: 의미 있고 증가하는 소수의 가계가 지속적인 월간 적자를 기록하며 자신들이 이용할 수 있는 가장 비싼 신용으로 이를 조달하고 있는 반면, 더 부유한 대차대조표가 지배하는 전체 통계는 이를 안정성으로 기록하고 있다는 점입니다.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## 다음에 주목해야 할 점

segments.src: For anyone tracking whether the split widens or narrows, a few indicators carry more information than the headline total:
segments.tr: 양극화가 확대되는지 좁혀지는지 추적하는 이들에게 몇 가지 지표는 헤드폰(헤드라인) 총계보다 더 많은 정보를 전달합니다:

segments.src: 1. **Transition-into-serious-delinquency rates by product**, especially cards and subprime auto — flows lead levels.
segments.tr: 1. **상품별 심각한 연체 진입률**, 특히 카드 및 서브프라임 자동차 대출 — 흐름이 수준을 선행합니다.

segments.src: 2. **Delinquency by credit-score tier and by age cohort.** Borrowers under 40 and those in the lowest score bands have shown the sharpest deterioration.
segments.tr: 2. **신용 점수 계층별 및 연령 코호트별 연체율.** 40세 미만의 차주들과 가장 낮은 점수대의 차주들이 가장 급격한 악화를 보였습니다.

segments.src: 3. **Revolving credit growth versus real disposable income growth.** When revolving credit outpaces income for consecutive quarters, the gap is being financed rather than closed.
segments.tr: 3. **회전 신용 증가율 대 실질 처분가능소득 증가율.** 회전 신용이 여러 분기 연속으로 소득을 앞지를 때, 그 격차는 메워지는 것이 아니라 조달되고 있는 것입니다.

segments.src: 4. **BNPL reporting coverage.** As more of these plans reach the bureaus, expect reported household debt to rise for mechanical reasons. That will be a measurement artifact, not necessarily new borrowing — and it will be widely misread as one.
segments.tr: 4. **BNPL 보고 커버리지.** 이러한 플랜들이 신용평가기관에 더 많이 도달함에 따라 기계적인 이유로 보고된 가계 부채가 증가할 것으로 예상하십시오. 이는 새로운 차입이 아니라 측정상의 인위적 결과일 것이며, 많은 이들이 이를 잘못 읽을 것입니다.

segments.src: 5. **The composition of what is being financed.** Essentials-driven credit growth and discretionary-driven credit growth carry very different implications for what follows.
segments.tr: 5. **자금이 조달되는 대상의 구성.** 필수품 중심의 신용 증가와 재량 소비 중심의 신용 증가는 그 이후에 일어날 일에 대해 매우 다른 시의적 함의를 가집니다.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 결론

segments.src: A record $18.8 trillion is not, by itself, alarming.
segments.tr: 기록적인 18조 8천억 달러 그 자체만으로는 경종을 울릴 일이 아닙니다.

segments.src: Household debt should grow with population, prices, and nominal income; records are the normal state of the series.
segments.tr: 가계 부채는 인구, 물가, 명목 소득과 함께 증가해야 하며, 기록 경신은 이 시계열의 정상적인 상태입니다.

segments.src: What deserves attention is the divergence the total conceals: one group of households retiring debt from a position of strength, another financing groceries at revolving rates because the alternative is going without.
segments.tr: 주목해야 할 것은 총계가 감추고 있는 괴리입니다. 한쪽 가계 그룹은 강력한 위치에서 부채를 청산하고 있는 반면, 다른 쪽은 대안이 없기 때문에 회전율 금리로 식료품비를 조달하고 있습니다.

segments.src: Both are inside the same number.
segments.tr: 둘 다 같은 숫자 안에 들어 있습니다.

segments.src: Only one of them is captured by the phrase "consumer balance sheets remain solid."
segments.tr: 그중 오직 하나만이 "소비자 대차대조표가 건전하다"는 문구에 포착됩니다.

segments.src: The averages are fine.
segments.tr: 평균은 괜찮습니다.

segments.src: The distribution is the story.
segments.tr: 분포가 바로 이야기의 핵심입니다.

segments.tr: *이 기사는 정보 제공만을 목적으로 하는 일반적인 경제 보도 및 논평입니다.

zh.title: 分期购买食品：美国18.8万亿美元债务堆栈内部的K型分化

segments.src: American household debt has reached a record of roughly **$18.8 trillion**, with about **$1.25 trillion** of that sitting on credit cards.
segments.tr: 美国家庭债务已达到约**18.8万亿美元**的历史新高，其中约有**1.25万亿美元**源于信用卡负债。

segments.src: Those are big, round, headline-friendly numbers — and, taken alone, they explain almost nothing.
segments.tr: 这些都是庞大、整齐且易于登上头条的数字——但单看这些数字，几乎无法解释任何问题。

segments.src: The more revealing detail is buried underneath.
segments.tr: 更具启发性的细节被掩盖在表象之下。

segments.src: Aggregate balances have largely flattened out.
segments.tr: 总体余额在很大程度上趋于平缓。

segments.src: Yet the share of card balances slipping into serious delinquency has stayed stubbornly close to levels the U.S.
segments.tr: 然而，陷入严重逾期的信用卡余额比例却顽固地接近美国在2008年金融危机之后不久几年里

segments.src: last saw in the years immediately following the 2008 financial crisis.
segments.tr: 最后一次看到的水平。

segments.src: Those two facts do not fit together comfortably.
segments.tr: 这两个事实并不能很好地契合在一起。

segments.src: Debt that is no longer growing quickly should not, in theory, be going bad at a rate reminiscent of a credit downturn.
segments.tr: 从理论上讲，不再快速增长的债务不应该以让人联想起信贷衰退的速度出现恶化。

segments.src: The explanation is that the national average is now describing two very different populations at once.
segments.tr: 对此的解释是，国家平均水平现在同时描述了两个截然不同的人群。

segments.src: ## The number that stopped moving, and the number that didn't
segments.tr: ## 停止变动的数字与没有停止变动的数字

segments.src: Quarterly household-debt data compiled by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York from a nationally representative sample of consumer credit reports gives the clearest public view of this.
segments.tr: 纽约联邦储备银行根据全国具有代表性的消费者信用报告样本编制的季度家庭债务数据，为我们提供了对此最清晰的公众视角。

segments.src: It tracks mortgages, auto loans, student loans, and credit cards — and, critically, it tracks *flows*: how much debt moved from current into 30-day, 90-day, and 120-day-plus delinquency each quarter.
segments.tr: 它追踪抵押贷款、汽车贷款、学生贷款和信用卡——至关重要的是，它追踪*资金流向*：每个季度有多少债务从正常状态转入30天、90天以及120天以上的逾期状态。

segments.src: Aggregate growth has cooled.
segments.tr: 总体增长已经冷却。

segments.src: Mortgage origination remains constrained by high rates and thin inventory.
segments.tr: 抵押贷款的发放仍然受到高利率和低库存的限制。

segments.src: Card balances, which climbed steeply through the post-pandemic period, have settled into a slower rhythm.
segments.tr: 在后疫情时期急剧攀升的信用卡余额，已经进入了一个较慢的节奏。

segments.src: On a chart of total balances, the last several quarters look almost calm.
segments.tr: 在总余额图表上，过去几个季度看起来几乎很平静。

segments.src: The transition rates do not look calm.
segments.tr: 但转型率看起来并不平静。

segments.src: The share of credit card balances moving into serious delinquency has hovered near post-2008 highs rather than normalizing back toward the mid-2010s baseline.
segments.tr: 进入严重逾期的信用卡余额比例一直在2008年后的高位附近徘徊，而没有向2010年代中期的基线回归。

segments.src: Auto loans show a related pattern, with subprime borrowers driving most of the deterioration.
segments.tr: 汽车贷款也呈现出相关模式，次贷借款人是恶化的主要驱动力。

segments.src: When balances flatten but delinquency transitions stay elevated, it usually means the composition of borrowing has shifted.
segments.tr: 当余额趋于平缓但逾期率仍然居高不下时，通常意味着借贷的构成发生了变化。

segments.src: Fewer people are adding debt — but the people still adding it are, on average, less able to service it.
segments.tr: 较少有人在增加债务——但仍在增加债务的人，平均而言偿债能力更差。

segments.src: ## What "K-shaped" actually means here
segments.tr: ## 这里的“K型”实际意味着什么

segments.src: The letter is a shorthand for divergence: one group's trajectory bending upward while another's bends down, from the same starting point.
segments.tr: 这个字母是分化的简写：从同一个起点出发，一个群体的轨迹向上弯曲，而另一个群体的轨迹向下弯曲。

segments.src: **The upper stroke.** Borrowers with prime and super-prime credit scores have been paying down revolving balances.
segments.tr: **上行分支。** 拥有优质（prime）和超优质（super-prime）信用评分的借款人一直在偿还循环债务。

segments.src: Many locked in mortgages at 3% or lower before 2022 and are effectively insulated from the rate cycle.
segments.tr: 许多人在2022年之前以3%或更低的利率锁定抵押贷款，实际上免受了利率周期的影响。

segments.src: Their financial assets have appreciated.
segments.tr: 他们的金融资产已经增值。

segments.src: For this group, higher interest rates have been closer to a feature than a bug — money-market yields and short-duration Treasuries have paid them to hold cash.
segments.tr: 对这一群体而言，更高的利率更像是一个特色而不是缺陷——货币市场收益率和短期国债一直在为他们持有现金支付报酬。

segments.src: They are deleveraging by choice, not necessity.
segments.tr: 他们是出于选择而非必要在进行去杠杆化。

segments.src: **The lower stroke.** Borrowers in the non-prime tiers are carrying more revolving debt at rates that, for many cards, sit above 20% APR.
segments.tr: **下行分支。** 次级（non-prime）梯队的借款人正在以对许多信用卡而言超过20%的年化利率（APR）承担更多的循环债务。

segments.src: They are far more likely to rent, which means the housing-cost lock-in that protected homeowners never applied to them.
segments.tr: 他们更有可能是租房者，这意味着保护了房主的住房成本锁定从未适用于他们。

segments.src: They have absorbed several years of cumulative price increases in groceries, insurance, utilities, and childcare on wages that, for many, rose but not by enough to close the gap.
segments.tr: 他们承受了多年来食品杂货、保险、公用事业和儿童保育方面不断累积的价格上涨，而许多人的工资虽然有所上涨，但幅度不足以弥补这一差距。

segments.src: Average them together and you get "household balance sheets are broadly healthy."
segments.tr: 将它们平均在一起，就会得出“家庭资产负债表总体健康”的结论。

segments.src: That statement is true of the aggregate and misleading about the distribution — which is precisely the problem with reading a $18.8 trillion figure as a single signal.
segments.tr: 这一陈述对总体而言是真实的，但对分布情况具有误导性——这正是将18.8万亿美元的数字视为单一信号的问题所在。

segments.src: ## The part that changes the character of the debt
segments.tr: ## 改变债务性质的部分

segments.src: Here is the shift that matters most, and it is qualitative rather than numerical.
segments.tr: 这里是最重要的转变，它是定性的而非数字的。

segments.src: Historically, revolving credit expanded fastest around discretionary consumption — electronics, travel, furniture, holiday spending.
segments.tr: 从历史上看，循环信用围绕着可自由支配的消费扩张最快——电子产品、旅游、家具、假日消费。

segments.src: Card debt was, broadly, a way to pull forward purchases that could otherwise have waited.
segments.tr: 广义上讲，信用卡债务是一种提前消费本可等待的购买行为的方式。

segments.src: A growing share of new non-prime borrowing now goes toward things that cannot wait.
segments.tr: 目前，新的次级借贷中越来越大的一比例用于无法等待的事物。

segments.src: Surveys from the Federal Reserve, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, and multiple consumer-finance researchers have documented households using credit cards and short-term installment products for groceries, rent, utility bills, insurance premiums, and medical costs.
segments.tr: 美联储、消费者金融保护局以及多位消费者金融研究人员的调查记录显示，家庭正在将信用卡和短期分期产品用于购买食品杂货、房租、公用事业账单、保险费和医疗费用。

segments.src: Buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) is the clearest illustration.
segments.tr: 先买后付（BNPL）是最清晰的例证。

segments.src: The product was built for mid-ticket discretionary retail — a jacket, a pair of headphones, a mattress.
segments.tr: 该产品专为中档可自由支配零售而设计——夹克、一副耳机、床垫。

segments.src: Its fastest-growing use cases increasingly include supermarket orders, food delivery, and everyday essentials split into four payments over six weeks.
segments.tr: 其增长最快的用例日益包括超市订单、外卖以及拆分为六周内四次付款的日常必需品。

segments.src: Debt used to smooth a shortfall behaves differently from debt used to accelerate a purchase.
segments.tr: 用于平抑资金短缺的债务与用于加速购买的债务表现不同。

segments.src: A television bought on credit is a one-time obligation.
segments.tr: 用信用购买的电视是一次性债务。

segments.src: Groceries bought on credit recur every week, which means the balance does not naturally retire itself — it compounds against a bill that arrives again in seven days.
segments.tr: 用信用购买的食品杂货每周都会重复，这意味着余额不会自然消失——它会针对七天后再次到来的账单不断复利。

segments.src: That is why the delinquency-transition series can stay elevated even as total balances plateau: the borrowing has become less about wants and more about the gap between a paycheck and a fixed monthly cost floor.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么逾期率序列可以在总余额趋于平稳的情况下保持高位：借贷越来越少地关乎欲望，而更多地关乎薪水与固定月度成本底线之间的差距。

segments.src: ## The measurement blind spot
segments.tr: ## 测量的盲点

segments.src: There is an important caveat that responsible readings of this data should include: **BNPL is only partially visible.**
segments.tr: 负责任地解读这些数据时应包含一个重要的注意事项：**BNPL只是部分可见的。**

segments.src: Most BNPL "pay-in-four" plans have historically not been furnished to the traditional credit bureaus in the same consistent way as cards and installment loans.
segments.tr: 从历史上看，大多数BNPL“四期付款”计划并未像信用卡和分期贷款那样以一致的方式提供给传统的信用局。

segments.src: Reporting practices have been changing, and major bureaus and lenders have moved toward incorporating this data — but the transition is uneven and recent.
segments.tr: 报告惯例一直在发生变化，各大信用局和贷款机构已朝着整合这些数据的方向迈进——但转型是不均衡且近期的。

segments.src: The practical consequence is that the official household-debt total almost certainly understates total consumer obligations, and that a household can appear less leveraged in bureau data than it actually is.
segments.tr: 实际结果是，官方的家庭债务总额几乎可以肯定低估了消费者的总债务，并且家庭在信用局数据中可能显得比实际杠杆率更低。

segments.src: It also creates "loan stacking" risk, where a borrower holds several concurrent plans from different providers, none of which can see the others.
segments.tr: 它还产生了“贷款叠加”（loan stacking）风险，即借款人持有来自不同提供商的多个同时进行的计划，而其中任何一个提供商都无法看到其他计划。

segments.src: This does not invalidate the $18.8 trillion figure.
segments.tr: 这并不否定18.8万亿美元的数字。

segments.src: It means the figure should be read as a floor for one category of borrowing, not a ceiling.
segments.tr: 这意味着该数字应被视为某一类借贷的底线，而不是天花板。

segments.src: ## Why aggregate stability can persist for a long time
segments.tr: ## 为什么总体稳定性可以长期持续

segments.src: It would be a mistake to read elevated card delinquencies as a forecast of systemic stress.
segments.tr: 将升高的信用卡逾期视为系统性压力预测将是一个错误。

segments.src: Several structural factors argue against a direct 2008 analogy:
segments.tr: 几个结构性因素不支持直接与2008年进行类比：

segments.src: - **Mortgage debt, the dominant component, is qualitatively different this cycle.** Post-crisis underwriting standards, the near-absence of the 2000s-era exotic products, and the enormous stock of fixed-rate loans originated below 4% make the largest slice of household debt unusually resilient.
segments.tr: - **抵押贷款债务是主导部分，在本周期中具有本质上的不同。** 危机后的承销标准、2000年代风格异国产品的几乎绝迹，以及以低于4%的利率发放的大量固定利率贷款存量，使最大份额的家庭债务异常具有韧性。

segments.src: - **Credit card debt is a small share of the total.** At roughly $1.25 trillion against $18.8 trillion, cards represent under 7% of household liabilities. Severe stress in that segment is painful for the households involved and manageable for the financial system.
segments.tr: - **信用卡债务只占总额的一小部分。** 在18.8万亿美元的总额中约占1.25万亿美元，信用卡占家庭负债的不到7%。该细分市场的严重压力对于所涉家庭来说是痛苦的，但对金融系统而言是可控的。

segments.src: - **Lenders have already adjusted.** Card issuers have tightened approval criteria, trimmed credit lines, and provisioned against losses over multiple quarters. The deterioration has not been a surprise to the institutions holding the exposure.
segments.tr: - **贷款机构已经进行了调整。** 信用卡发行商收紧了审批标准，削减了信用额度，并在多个季度内为损失计提了拨备。对于持有敞口的机构而言，这种恶化并非意料之外。

segments.src: The realistic reading is not "crisis pending."
segments.tr: 现实的解读不是“危机即将来临”。

segments.src: It is that a meaningful and growing minority of households are running a persistent monthly deficit and financing it with the most expensive credit available to them — while the aggregate statistics, dominated by wealthier balance sheets, register that as stability.
segments.tr: 而是有意义且不断增加的少数家庭正在运行持续的月度赤字，并用他们能获得的最高成本信贷来为其融资——而由更富裕的资产负债表主导的总体统计数据却将其记录为稳定性。

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## 接下来需要关注什么

segments.src: For anyone tracking whether the split widens or narrows, a few indicators carry more information than the headline total:
segments.tr: 对于任何追踪分化是扩大还是缩小的人来说，几个指标比头条总额包含更多信息：

segments.src: 1. **Transition-into-serious-delinquency rates by product**, especially cards and subprime auto — flows lead levels.
segments.tr: 1. **按产品划分的严重逾期率**，尤其是信用卡和次级汽车贷款——资金流向领先于水平。

segments.src: 2. **Delinquency by credit-score tier and by age cohort.** Borrowers under 40 and those in the lowest score bands have shown the sharpest deterioration.
segments.tr: 2. **按信用评分层级和年龄群体的逾期情况。** 40岁以下的借款人和评分最低的群体表现出最急剧的恶化。

segments.src: 3. **Revolving credit growth versus real disposable income growth.** When revolving credit outpaces income for consecutive quarters, the gap is being financed rather than closed.
segments.tr: 3. **循环信贷增长与实际可支配收入增长的对比。** 当循环信贷连续几个季度超过收入时，这一差距是在通过融资来维持，而不是在缩小。

segments.src: 4. **BNPL reporting coverage.** As more of these plans reach the bureaus, expect reported household debt to rise for mechanical reasons. That will be a measurement artifact, not necessarily new borrowing — and it will be widely misread as one.
segments.tr: 4. **BNPL报告覆盖率。** 随着更多此类计划进入信用局，出于机械原因，预计报告的家庭债务将会上升。这将是一个测量人工产物，不一定代表新的借贷——并且它将被广泛误解为新借贷。

segments.src: 5. **The composition of what is being financed.** Essentials-driven credit growth and discretionary-driven credit growth carry very different implications for what follows.
segments.tr: 5. **正在融资的消费构成。** 必需品驱动的信贷增长与可自由支配品驱动的信贷增长，对后续发展具有截然不同的含义。

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 底线

segments.src: A record $18.8 trillion is not, by itself, alarming.
segments.tr: 创纪录的18.8万亿美元本身并不令人震惊。

segments.src: Household debt should grow with population, prices, and nominal income; records are the normal state of the series.
segments.tr: 家庭债务应当随着人口、物价和名义收入而增长；创纪录是该序列的正常状态。

segments.src: What deserves attention is the divergence the total conceals: one group of households retiring debt from a position of strength, another financing groceries at revolving rates because the alternative is going without.
segments.tr: 值得关注的是总量所掩盖的分化：一个家庭群体从实力地位出发偿还债务，另一个群体则因为别无选择而以循环利率为食品杂货融资。

segments.src: Both are inside the same number.
segments.tr: 两者都包含在同一个数字中。

segments.src: Only one of them is captured by the phrase "consumer balance sheets remain solid."
segments.tr: 其中只有一小部分被“消费者资产负债表保持稳固”这一短语所捕捉。

segments.src: The averages are fine.
segments.tr: 平均值很好。

segments.src: The distribution is the story.
segments.tr: 分布才是故事所在。

hi.title: किस्तों में किराने का सामान: अमेरिका के $18.8 ट्रिलियन के कर्ज के ढेर के भीतर के-आकार का विभाजन

segments.src: American household debt has reached a record of roughly **$18.8 trillion**, with about **$1.25 trillion** of that sitting on credit cards.
segments.tr: अमेरिकी घरेलू कर्ज रिकॉर्ड लगभग **$18.8 ट्रिलियन** तक पहुंच गया है, जिसमें से लगभग **$1.25 ट्रिलियन** क्रेडिट कार्ड पर है।

segments.src: Those are big, round, headline-friendly numbers — and, taken alone, they explain almost nothing.
segments.tr: ये बड़े, गोल, हेडलाइन के अनुकूल आंकड़े हैं - और, अकेले लेने पर, वे लगभग कुछ भी नहीं समझाते हैं।

segments.src: The more revealing detail is buried underneath.
segments.tr: अधिक खुलासा करने वाला विवरण नीचे दबा हुआ है।

segments.src: Aggregate balances have largely flattened out.
segments.tr: समग्र शेष राशि काफी हद तक समतल हो गई है।

segments.src: Yet the share of card balances slipping into serious delinquency has stayed stubbornly close to levels the U.S.
segments.tr: फिर भी गंभीर चूक में फिसलने वाले कार्ड शेष का हिस्सा जिद्दी रूप से उन स्तरों के करीब बना हुआ है जो यू.एस.

segments.src: last saw in the years immediately following the 2008 financial crisis.
segments.tr: ने आखिरी बार 2008 के वित्तीय संकट के तुरंत बाद के वर्षों में देखा था।

segments.src: Those two facts do not fit together comfortably.
segments.tr: वे दोनों तथ्य आराम से एक साथ फिट नहीं होते हैं।

segments.src: Debt that is no longer growing quickly should not, in theory, be going bad at a rate reminiscent of a credit downturn.
segments.tr: जो कर्ज अब तेजी से नहीं बढ़ रहा है, उसे सिद्धांत रूप में, क्रेडिट मंदी की याद दिलाने वाली दर से खराब नहीं होना चाहिए।

segments.src: The explanation is that the national average is now describing two very different populations at once.
segments.tr: स्पष्टीकरण यह है कि राष्ट्रीय औसत अब एक ही बार में दो बहुत अलग आबादी का वर्णन कर रहा है।

segments.src: ## The number that stopped moving, and the number that didn't
segments.tr: ## वह संख्या जो बढ़ना बंद हो गई, और वह संख्या जो नहीं रुकी

segments.src: Quarterly household-debt data compiled by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York from a nationally representative sample of consumer credit reports gives the clearest public view of this.
segments.tr: फेडरल रिजर्व बैंक ऑफ न्यूयॉर्क द्वारा उपभोक्ता क्रेडिट रिपोर्टों के राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर प्रतिनिधि नमूने से संकलित त्रैमासिक घरेलू-ऋण डेटा इसका सबसे स्पष्ट सार्वजनिक दृष्टिकोण देता है।

segments.src: It tracks mortgages, auto loans, student loans, and credit cards — and, critically, it tracks *flows*: how much debt moved from current into 30-day, 90-day, and 120-day-plus delinquency each quarter.
segments.tr: यह बंधक, ऑटो ऋण, छात्र ऋण और क्रेडिट कार्ड को ट्रैक करता है — और, गंभीर रूप से, यह *प्रवाह* को ट्रैक करता है: प्रत्येक तिमाही में कितना ऋण वर्तमान से 30-दिन, 90-दिन और 120-दिन-प्लस चूक में चला गया।

segments.src: Aggregate growth has cooled.
segments.tr: समग्र वृद्धि ठंडी हो गई है।

segments.src: Mortgage origination remains constrained by high rates and thin inventory.
segments.tr: मॉर्गेज ओरिजिनेशन उच्च दरों और कम इन्वेंट्री द्वारा प्रतिबंधित रहता है।

segments.src: Card balances, which climbed steeply through the post-pandemic period, have settled into a slower rhythm.
segments.tr: कार्ड का शेष, जो महामारी के बाद की अवधि में तेजी से चढ़ गया था, एक धीमी गति में बस गया है।

segments.src: On a chart of total balances, the last several quarters look almost calm.
segments.tr: कुल शेष के चार्ट पर, पिछले कई क्वार्टर लगभग शांत दिखते हैं।

segments.src: The transition rates do not look calm.
segments.tr: संक्रमण दरें शांत नहीं दिखती हैं।

segments.src: The share of credit card balances moving into serious delinquency has hovered near post-2008 highs rather than normalizing back toward the mid-2010s baseline.
segments.tr: गंभीर चूक में जाने वाले क्रेडिट कार्ड शेष का हिस्सा 2010 के दशक के मध्य के आधार रेखा की ओर सामान्य होने के बजाय 2008 के बाद के उच्च स्तर के करीब मंडरा रहा है।

segments.src: Auto loans show a related pattern, with subprime borrowers driving most of the deterioration.
segments.tr: ऑटो ऋण एक संबंधित पैटर्न दिखाते हैं, जिसमें सबप्राइम उधारकर्ता अधिकांश गिरावट को चला रहे हैं।

segments.src: When balances flatten but delinquency transitions stay elevated, it usually means the composition of borrowing has shifted.
segments.tr: जब शेष समतल हो जाते हैं लेकिन चूक के संक्रमण ऊंचे रहते हैं, तो इसका आमतौर पर मतलब होता है कि उधार की संरचना बदल गई है।

segments.src: Fewer people are adding debt — but the people still adding it are, on average, less able to service it.
segments.tr: कम लोग ऋण जोड़ रहे हैं - लेकिन जो लोग अभी भी इसे जोड़ रहे हैं, औसतन, इसे चुकाने में कम सक्षम हैं।

segments.src: ## What "K-shaped" actually means here
segments.tr: ## यहाँ "के-आकार" का वास्तव में क्या अर्थ है

segments.src: The letter is a shorthand for divergence: one group's trajectory bending upward while another's bends down, from the same starting point.
segments.tr: यह अक्षर विचलन के लिए एक संक्षिप्त रूप है: एक समूह का प्रक्षेपवक्र ऊपर की ओर झुकना जबकि दूसरे का नीचे की ओर झुकना, एक ही शुरुआती बिंदु से।

segments.src: **The upper stroke.** Borrowers with prime and super-prime credit scores have been paying down revolving balances.
segments.tr: **ऊपरी स्ट्रोक।** प्राइम और सुपर-प्राइम क्रेडिट स्कोर वाले उधारकर्ता रिवॉल्विंग बैलेंस का भुगतान कर रहे हैं।

segments.src: Many locked in mortgages at 3% or lower before 2022 and are effectively insulated from the rate cycle.
segments.tr: कई लोगों ने 2022 से पहले 3% या उससे कम पर मॉर्गेज लॉक कर दिया था और दर चक्र से प्रभावी रूप से सुरक्षित हैं।

segments.src: Their financial assets have appreciated.
segments.tr: उनकी वित्तीय संपत्ति की सराहना हुई है।

segments.src: For this group, higher interest rates have been closer to a feature than a bug — money-market yields and short-duration Treasuries have paid them to hold cash.
segments.tr: इस समूह के लिए, उच्च ब्याज दरें एक बग की तुलना में एक सुविधा के करीब रही हैं - मनी-मार्केट यील्ड और अल्पकालिक ट्रेजरी ने उन्हें नकदी रखने के लिए भुगतान किया है।

segments.src: They are deleveraging by choice, not necessity.
segments.tr: वे मजबूरी से नहीं, बल्कि अपनी मर्जी से डीलेवरिंग कर रहे हैं।

segments.src: **The lower stroke.** Borrowers in the non-prime tiers are carrying more revolving debt at rates that, for many cards, sit above 20% APR.
segments.tr: **निचला स्ट्रोक।** गैर-प्राइम टियर के उधारकर्ता ऐसी दरों पर अधिक रिवॉल्विंग ऋण ले जा रहे हैं जो कई कार्डों के लिए 20% APR से ऊपर हैं।

segments.src: They are far more likely to rent, which means the housing-cost lock-in that protected homeowners never applied to them.
segments.tr: उनके किराए पर लेने की संभावना अधिक होती है, जिसका अर्थ है कि आवास-लागत लॉक-इन जिसने घर के मालिकों की रक्षा की, उन पर कभी लागू नहीं हुआ।

segments.src: They have absorbed several years of cumulative price increases in groceries, insurance, utilities, and childcare on wages that, for many, rose but not by enough to close the gap.
segments.tr: उन्होंने किराने, बीमा, उपयोगिताओं और चाइल्डकैअर में संचयी मूल्य वृद्धि के कई वर्षों को ऐसे वेतन पर अवशोषित किया है जो कई लोगों के लिए बढ़ा, लेकिन अंतर को पाटने के लिए पर्याप्त नहीं था।

segments.src: Average them together and you get "household balance sheets are broadly healthy."
segments.tr: उन्हें एक साथ औसत करें और आपको "घरेलू बैलेंस शीट मोटे तौर पर स्वस्थ हैं" मिलता है।

segments.src: That statement is true of the aggregate and misleading about the distribution — which is precisely the problem with reading a $18.8 trillion figure as a single signal.
segments.tr: यह बयान कुल के लिए सच है और वितरण के बारे में भ्रामक है - जो कि एक एकल संकेत के रूप में $18.8 ट्रिलियन के आंकड़े को पढ़ने की समस्या है।

segments.src: ## The part that changes the character of the debt
segments.tr: ## वह हिस्सा जो ऋण के चरित्र को बदल देता है

segments.src: Here is the shift that matters most, and it is qualitative rather than numerical.
segments.tr: यहाँ वह बदलाव है जो सबसे अधिक मायने रखता है, और यह संख्यात्मक के बजाय गुणात्मक है।

segments.src: Historically, revolving credit expanded fastest around discretionary consumption — electronics, travel, furniture, holiday spending.
segments.tr: ऐतिहासिक रूप से, विवेकाधीन उपभोग के इर्द-गिर्द रिवॉल्विंग क्रेडिट सबसे तेजी से बढ़ा — इलेक्ट्रॉनिक्स, यात्रा, फर्नीचर, छुट्टी का खर्च।

segments.src: Card debt was, broadly, a way to pull forward purchases that could otherwise have waited.
segments.tr: कार्ड का कर्ज, मोटे तौर पर, उन खरीद को आगे बढ़ाने का एक तरीका था जो अन्यथा इंतजार कर सकते थे।

segments.src: A growing share of new non-prime borrowing now goes toward things that cannot wait.
segments.tr: नए गैर-प्राइम उधार का एक बढ़ता हुआ हिस्सा अब उन चीजों की ओर जाता है जो इंतजार नहीं कर सकती हैं।

segments.src: Surveys from the Federal Reserve, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, and multiple consumer-finance researchers have documented households using credit cards and short-term installment products for groceries, rent, utility bills, insurance premiums, and medical costs.
segments.tr: फेडरल रिजर्व, कंज्यू머 फाइनेंशियल प्रोटेक्शन ब्यूरो और कई उपभोक्ता-वित्त शोधकर्ताओं के सर्वेक्षणों ने किराने के सामान, किराए, उपयोगिता बिलों, बीमा प्रीमियम और चिकित्सा लागतों के लिए क्रेडिट कार्ड और अल्पकालिक किस्त उत्पादों का उपयोग करने वाले परिवारों का दस्तावेजीकरण किया है।

segments.src: Buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) is the clearest illustration.
segments.tr: बाय-नाउ-पे-लेटर (BNPL) सबसे स्पष्ट उदाहरण है।

segments.src: The product was built for mid-ticket discretionary retail — a jacket, a pair of headphones, a mattress.
segments.tr: उत्पाद को मिड-टिकट विवेकाधीन खुदरा बिक्री के लिए बनाया गया था - एक जैकेट, हेडफ़ोन की एक जोड़ी, एक गद्दा।

segments.src: Its fastest-growing use cases increasingly include supermarket orders, food delivery, and everyday essentials split into four payments over six weeks.
segments.tr: इसके सबसे तेजी से बढ़ते उपयोग के मामलों में तेजी से सुपरमार्केट ऑर्डर, फूड डिलीवरी और छह सप्ताह में चार भुगतानों में विभाजित हर रोज के आवश्यक सामान शामिल हैं।

segments.src: Debt used to smooth a shortfall behaves differently from debt used to accelerate a purchase.
segments.tr: कमी को पाटने के लिए उपयोग किया जाने वाला ऋण खरीद को गति देने के लिए उपयोग किए जाने वाले ऋण से अलग व्यवहार करता है।

segments.src: A television bought on credit is a one-time obligation.
segments.tr: क्रेडिट पर खरीदा गया टेलीविज़न एक बार का दायित्व है।

segments.src: Groceries bought on credit recur every week, which means the balance does not naturally retire itself — it compounds against a bill that arrives again in seven days.
segments.tr: क्रेडिट पर खरीदा गया किराने का सामान हर हफ्ते दोहराता है, जिसका अर्थ है कि शेष राशि स्वाभाविक रूप से खुद को सेवानिवृत्त नहीं करती है - यह एक ऐसे बिल के खिलाफ यौगिक करती है जो सात दिनों में फिर से आता है।

segments.src: That is why the delinquency-transition series can stay elevated even as total balances plateau: the borrowing has become less about wants and more about the gap between a paycheck and a fixed monthly cost floor.
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि चूक-संक्रमण श्रृंखला ऊंची रह सकती है, भले ही कुल शेष पठार हो जाए: उधार लेने से कम हो गया है और पेचेक और एक निश्चित मासिक लागत तल के बीच की खाई के बारे में अधिक हो गया है।

segments.src: ## The measurement blind spot
segments.tr: ## माप अंधा स्थान

segments.src: There is an important caveat that responsible readings of this data should include: **BNPL is only partially visible.**
segments.tr: एक महत्वपूर्ण चेतावनी है जिसे इस डेटा के जिम्मेदार रीडिंग में शामिल करना चाहिए: **BNPL केवल आंशिक रूप से दिखाई दे रहा है।**

segments.src: Most BNPL "pay-in-four" plans have historically not been furnished to the traditional credit bureaus in the same consistent way as cards and installment loans.
segments.tr: अधिकांश BNPL "पे-इन-फोर" योजनाओं को ऐतिहासिक रूप से कार्ड और किस्त ऋणों के समान लगातार तरीके से पारंपरिक क्रेडिट ब्यूरो को सुसज्जित नहीं किया गया है।

segments.src: Reporting practices have been changing, and major bureaus and lenders have moved toward incorporating this data — but the transition is uneven and recent.
segments.tr: रिपोर्टिंग अभ्यास बदल रहे हैं, और प्रमुख ब्यूरो और ऋणदाता इस डेटा को शामिल करने की ओर बढ़ गए हैं - लेकिन संक्रमण असमान और हालिया है।

segments.src: The practical consequence is that the official household-debt total almost certainly understates total consumer obligations, and that a household can appear less leveraged in bureau data than it actually is.
segments.tr: व्यावहारिक परिणाम यह है कि आधिकारिक घरेलू-ऋण कुल लगभग निश्चित रूप से कुल उपभोक्ता दायित्वों को कम आंकता है, और यह कि एक घरेलू ब्यूरो डेटा में कम लीवरेज दिखाई दे सकता है जितना वह वास्तव में है।

segments.src: It also creates "loan stacking" risk, where a borrower holds several concurrent plans from different providers, none of which can see the others.
segments.tr: यह "लोन स्टैकिंग" जोखिम भी पैदा करता है, जहाँ एक उधारकर्ता के पास अलग-अलग प्रदाताओं से कई समवर्ती योजनाएं होती हैं, जिनमें से कोई भी दूसरे को नहीं देख सकती है।

segments.src: This does not invalidate the $18.8 trillion figure.
segments.tr: यह $18.8 ट्रिलियन के आंकड़े को अमान्य नहीं करता है।

segments.src: It means the figure should be read as a floor for one category of borrowing, not a ceiling.
segments.tr: इसका मतलब है कि आंकड़े को उधार की एक श्रेणी के लिए फर्श के रूप में पढ़ा जाना चाहिए, छत के रूप में नहीं।

segments.src: ## Why aggregate stability can persist for a long time
segments.tr: ## समग्र स्थिरता लंबे समय तक क्यों बनी रह सकती है

segments.src: It would be a mistake to read elevated card delinquencies as a forecast of systemic stress.
segments.tr: ऊंचे कार्ड डिफॉल्ट को प्रणालीगत तनाव के पूर्वानुमान के रूप में पढ़ना एक गलती होगी।

segments.src: Several structural factors argue against a direct 2008 analogy:
segments.tr: कई संरचनात्मक कारक प्रत्यक्ष 2008 सादृश्य के खिलाफ बहस करते हैं:

segments.src: - **Mortgage debt, the dominant component, is qualitatively different this cycle.** Post-crisis underwriting standards, the near-absence of the 2000s-era exotic products, and the enormous stock of fixed-rate loans originated below 4% make the largest slice of household debt unusually resilient.
segments.tr: - **मॉर्गेज ऋण, प्रमुख घटक, इस चक्र में गुणात्मक रूप से अलग है।** संकट के बाद के हामीदारी मानक, 2000 के दशक के विदेशी उत्पादों की लगभग अनुपस्थिति, और 4% से नीचे उत्पन्न निश्चित दर वाले ऋणों का भारी स्टॉक घरेलू ऋण के सबसे बड़े हिस्से को असामान्य रूप से लचीला बनाता है।

segments.src: - **Credit card debt is a small share of the total.** At roughly $1.25 trillion against $18.8 trillion, cards represent under 7% of household liabilities. Severe stress in that segment is painful for the households involved and manageable for the financial system.
segments.tr: - **क्रेडिट कार्ड ऋण कुल का एक छोटा सा हिस्सा है।** $18.8 ट्रिलियन के मुकाबले लगभग $1.25 ट्रिलियन पर, कार्ड घरेलू देनदारियों का 7% से कम प्रतिनिधित्व करते हैं। उस खंड में गंभीर तनाव शामिल परिवारों के लिए दर्दनाक है और वित्तीय प्रणाली के लिए प्रबंधनीय है।

segments.src: - **Lenders have already adjusted.** Card issuers have tightened approval criteria, trimmed credit lines, and provisioned against losses over multiple quarters. The deterioration has not been a surprise to the institutions holding the exposure.
segments.tr: - **ऋणदाता पहले ही समायोजित कर चुके हैं।** कार्ड जारीकर्ताओं ने अनुमोदन मानदंडों को कड़ा कर दिया है, क्रेडिट लाइनों को ट्रिम किया है, और कई तिमाहियों में नुकसान के खिलाफ प्रावधान किया है। जोखिम रखने वाली संस्थाओं के लिए गिरावट कोई आश्चर्य की बात नहीं रही है।

segments.src: The realistic reading is not "crisis pending."
segments.tr: यथार्थवादी पढ़ना "संकट लंबित" नहीं है।

segments.src: It is that a meaningful and growing minority of households are running a persistent monthly deficit and financing it with the most expensive credit available to them — while the aggregate statistics, dominated by wealthier balance sheets, register that as stability.
segments.tr: यह है कि परिवारों का एक सार्थक और बढ़ता हुआ अल्पसंख्यक एक लगातार मासिक घाटा चला रहा है और इसे उनके लिए उपलब्ध सबसे महंगे क्रेडिट के साथ वित्तपोषित कर रहा है - जबकि समग्र आंकड़े, अमीर बैलेंस शीट द्वारा हावी हैं, इसे स्थिरता के रूप में पंजीकृत करते हैं।

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## आगे क्या देखना है

segments.src: For anyone tracking whether the split widens or narrows, a few indicators carry more information than the headline total:
segments.tr: यह ट्रैक करने वाले किसी भी व्यक्ति के लिए कि विभाजन चौड़ा होता है या संकीर्ण होता है, कुछ संकेतक हेडलाइन कुल की तुलना में अधिक जानकारी लेते हैं:

segments.src: 1. **Transition-into-serious-delinquency rates by product**, especially cards and subprime auto — flows lead levels.
segments.tr: 1. **उत्पाद द्वारा गंभीर-चूक की दर में संक्रमण**, विशेष रूप से कार्ड और सबप्राइम ऑटो - प्रवाह स्तर का नेतृत्व करते हैं।

segments.src: 2. **Delinquency by credit-score tier and by age cohort.** Borrowers under 40 and those in the lowest score bands have shown the sharpest deterioration.
segments.tr: **क्रेडिट-स्कोर टियर और आयु समूह द्वारा चूक।** 40 वर्ष से कम उम्र के उधारकर्ताओं और सबसे कम स्कोर बैंड में रहने वालों ने सबसे तेज गिरावट दिखाई है।

segments.src: 3. **Revolving credit growth versus real disposable income growth.** When revolving credit outpaces income for consecutive quarters, the gap is being financed rather than closed.
segments.tr: **वास्तविक प्रयोज्य आय वृद्धि बनाम रिवॉल्विंग क्रेडिट वृद्धि।** जब लगातार तिमाहियों के लिए आय से अधिक रिवॉल्विंग क्रेडिट होता है, तो अंतर को पाटने के बजाय वित्तपोषित किया जा रहा है।

segments.src: 4. **BNPL reporting coverage.** As more of these plans reach the bureaus, expect reported household debt to rise for mechanical reasons. That will be a measurement artifact, not necessarily new borrowing — and it will be widely misread as one.
segments.tr: **BNPL रिपोर्टिंग कवरेज।** चूंकि इनमें से अधिक योजनाएं ब्यूरो तक पहुंचती हैं, इसलिए यांत्रिक कारणों से रिपोर्ट किए गए घरेलू ऋण में वृद्धि की उम्मीद है। वह एक माप कलाकृती होगी, जरूरी नहीं कि नया उधार हो - और इसे व्यापक रूप से एक के रूप में गलत पढ़ा जाएगा।

segments.src: 5. **The composition of what is being financed.** Essentials-driven credit growth and discretionary-driven credit growth carry very different implications for what follows.
segments.tr: **वित्त पोषित होने वाली चीजों की संरचना।** आवश्यक-संचालित क्रेडिट वृद्धि और विवेकाधीन-संचालित क्रेडिट वृद्धि के बाद क्या होता है, इसके लिए बहुत अलग निहितार्थ हैं।

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## निचला रेखा

segments.src: A record $18.8 trillion is not, by itself, alarming.
segments.tr: एक रिकॉर्ड $18.8 ट्रिलियन अपने आप में अलार्मिंग नहीं है।

segments.src: Household debt should grow with population, prices, and nominal income; records are the normal state of the series.
segments.tr: घरेलू ऋण को जनसंख्या, कीमतों और नाममात्र आय के साथ बढ़ना चाहिए; रिकॉर्ड श्रृंखला की सामान्य स्थिति हैं।

segments.src: What deserves attention is the divergence the total conceals: one group of households retiring debt from a position of strength, another financing groceries at revolving rates because the alternative is going without.
segments.tr: जो ध्यान देने योग्य है वह विचलन है जिसे कुल छुपाता है: परिवारों का एक समूह ताकत की स्थिति से ऋण सेवानिवृत्त कर रहा है, दूसरा रिवॉल्विंग दरों पर किराने का सामान वित्तपोषित कर रहा है क्योंकि विकल्प बिना के जाना है।

segments.src: Both are inside the same number.
segments.tr: दोनों एक ही संख्या के अंदर हैं।

segments.src: Only one of them is captured by the phrase "consumer balance sheets remain solid."
segments.tr: उनमें से केवल एक को "उपभोक्ता बैलेंस शीट ठोस बनी हुई है" वाक्यांश द्वारा कब्जा कर लिया गया है।

segments.src: The averages are fine.
segments.tr: औसत ठीक हैं।

segments.src: The distribution is the story.
segments.tr: वितरण ही कहानी है।

segments.src: *This article is general economic reporting and commentary for informational purposes only.
segments.tr: *यह लेख केवल सूचना के उद्देश्यों के लिए सामान्य आर्थिक रिपोर्टिंग और टिप्पणी है।

segments.src: It is not financial, investment, tax, or legal advice, and it is not a recommendation regarding any credit product or provider.
segments.tr: यह वित्तीय, निवेश, कर या कानूनी सलाह नहीं है, और यह किसी भी क्रेडिट उत्पाद या प्रदाता के संबंध में कोई सिफारिश नहीं है।

segments.src: Figures cited reflect publicly reported data at the time of writing; readers should consult the most recent releases from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and other primary sources for current numbers, and consult a qualified professional about their own circumstances.*
segments.tr: उद्धृत आंकड़े लेखन के समय सार्वजनिक रूप से रिपोर्ट किए गए डेटा को दर्शाते हैं; पाठकों को वर्तमान संख्याओं के लिए फेडरल रिजर्व बैंक ऑफ न्यूयॉर्क और अन्य प्राथमिक स्रोतों से नवीनतम रिलीज़ से परामर्श करना चाहिए, और अपनी परिस्थितियों के बारे में किसी योग्य पेशेवर से परामर्श करना चाहिए।*

es.title: Comestibles a plazos: La división en forma de K dentro de la pila de deuda de $18.8 billones de EE. UU.

segments.src: American household debt has reached a record of roughly **$18.8 trillion**, with about **$1.25 trillion** of that sitting on credit cards.
segments.tr: La deuda de los hogares estadounidenses ha alcanzado un récord de aproximadamente **$18.8 billones**, con alrededor de **$1.25 billones** de eso en tarjetas de crédito.

segments.src: Those are big, round, headline-friendly numbers — and, taken alone, they explain almost nothing.
segments.tr: Esos son números grandes, redondos y amigables con los titulares, y, tomados solos, no explican casi nada.

segments.src: The more revealing detail is buried underneath.
segments.tr: El detalle más revelador está enterrado debajo.

segments.src: Aggregate balances have largely flattened out.
segments.tr: Los saldos agregados se han aplanado en gran medida.

segments.src: Yet the share of card balances slipping into serious delinquency has stayed stubbornly close to levels the U.S.
segments.tr: Sin embargo, la proporción de saldos de tarjetas que caen en delincuencia grave se ha mantenido obstinadamente cerca de los niveles que Estados Unidos

segments.src: last saw in the years immediately following the 2008 financial crisis.
segments.tr: vio por última vez en los años inmediatamente posteriores a la crisis financiera de 2008.

segments.src: Those two facts do not fit together comfortably.
segments.tr: Esos dos hechos no encajan cómodamente.

segments.src: Debt that is no longer growing quickly should not, in theory, be going bad at a rate reminiscent of a credit downturn.
segments.tr: La deuda que ya no crece rápidamente no debería, en teoría, estar empeorando a un ritmo que recuerde a una recesión crediticia.

segments.src: The explanation is that the national average is now describing two very different populations at once.
segments.tr: La explicación es que el promedio nacional ahora está describiendo a dos poblaciones muy diferentes a la vez.

segments.src: ## The number that stopped moving, and the number that didn't
segments.tr: ## El número que dejó de moverse y el número que no

segments.src: Quarterly household-debt data compiled by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York from a nationally representative sample of consumer credit reports gives the clearest public view of this.
segments.tr: Los datos trimestrales de la deuda de los hogares compilados por el Banco de la Reserva Federal de Nueva York a partir de una muestra representativa a nivel nacional de informes de crédito al consumo ofrecen la visión pública más clara de esto.

segments.src: It tracks mortgages, auto loans, student loans, and credit cards — and, critically, it tracks *flows*: how much debt moved from current into 30-day, 90-day, and 120-day-plus delinquency each quarter.
segments.tr: Rastrea hipotecas, préstamos para automóviles, préstamos estudiantiles y tarjetas de crédito, y, de manera crítica, rastrea los *flujos*: cuánta deuda pasó de corriente a delincuencia de 30 días, 90 días y 120 días o más cada trimestre.

segments.src: Aggregate growth has cooled.
segments.tr: El crecimiento agregado se ha enfriado.

segments.src: Mortgage origination remains constrained by high rates and thin inventory.
segments.tr: La originación de hipotecas sigue limitada por las altas tasas y el inventario escaso.

segments.src: Card balances, which climbed steeply through the post-pandemic period, have settled into a slower rhythm.
segments.tr: Los saldos de las tarjetas, que subieron fuertemente durante el período posterior a la pandemia, se han asentado en un ritmo más lento.

segments.src: On a chart of total balances, the last several quarters look almost calm.
segments.tr: En un gráfico de saldos totales, los últimos trimestres parecen casi tranquilos.

segments.src: The transition rates do not look calm.
segments.tr: Las tasas de transición no parecen tranquilas.

segments.src: The share of credit card balances moving into serious delinquency has hovered near post-2008 highs rather than normalizing back toward the mid-2010s baseline.
segments.tr: La proporción de saldos de tarjetas de crédito que pasan a una delincuencia grave se ha mantenido cerca de los máximos posteriores a 2008 en lugar de normalizarse hacia la línea de base de mediados de la década de 2010.

segments.src: Auto loans show a related pattern, with subprime borrowers driving most of the deterioration.
segments.tr: Los préstamos para automóviles muestran un patrón relacionado, con los prestatarios de alto riesgo impulsando la mayor parte del deterioro.

segments.src: When balances flatten but delinquency transitions stay elevated, it usually means the composition of borrowing has shifted.
segments.tr: Cuando los saldos se tapan pero las transiciones de delincuencia se mantienen elevadas, generalmente significa que la composición del endeudamiento ha cambiado.

segments.src: Fewer people are adding debt — but the people still adding it are, on average, less able to service it.
segments.tr: Menos personas están agregando deuda, pero las personas que aún la agregan son, en promedio, menos capaces de pagarla.

segments.src: ## What "K-shaped" actually means here
segments.tr: ## Lo que significa realmente "en forma de K" aquí

segments.src: The letter is a shorthand for divergence: one group's trajectory bending upward while another's bends down, from the same starting point.
segments.tr: La letra es una abreviatura de divergencia: la trayectoria de un grupo se curva hacia arriba mientras que la de otro se curva hacia abajo, desde el mismo punto de partida.

segments.src: **The upper stroke.** Borrowers with prime and super-prime credit scores have been paying down revolving balances.
segments.tr: **El trazo superior.** Los prestatarios con puntajes de crédito prime y super-prime han estado pagando saldos revolventes.

segments.src: Many locked in mortgages at 3% or lower before 2022 and are effectively insulated from the rate cycle.
segments.tr: Muchos aseguraron hipotecas al 3% o menos antes de 2022 y están efectivamente aislados del ciclo de tasas.

segments.src: Their financial assets have appreciated.
segments.tr: Sus activos financieros se han apreciado.

segments.src: For this group, higher interest rates have been closer to a feature than a bug — money-market yields and short-duration Treasuries have paid them to hold cash.
segments.tr: Para este grupo, las tasas de interés más altas han estado más cerca de una característica que de un error: los rendimientos de los fondos del mercado monetario y los bonos del Tesoro a corto plazo les han pagado por mantener efectivo.

segments.src: They are deleveraging by choice, not necessity.
segments.tr: Se están desapalancando por elección, no por necesidad.

segments.src: **The lower stroke.** Borrowers in the non-prime tiers are carrying more revolving debt at rates that, for many cards, sit above 20% APR.
segments.tr: **El trazo inferior.** Los prestatarios en los niveles no prime llevan más deuda revolvente a tasas que, para muchas tarjetas, se sitúan por encima del 20% APR.

segments.src: They are far more likely to rent, which means the housing-cost lock-in that protected homeowners never applied to them.
segments.tr: Es mucho más probable que alquilen, lo que significa que el bloqueo de los costos de la vivienda que protegió a los propietarios nunca se aplicó a ellos.

segments.src: They have absorbed several years of cumulative price increases in groceries, insurance, utilities, and childcare on wages that, for many, rose but not by enough to close the gap.
segments.tr: Han absorbido varios años de aumentos acumulativos de precios en comestibles, seguros, servicios públicos y cuidado infantil con salarios que, para muchos, aumentaron pero no lo suficiente como para cerrar la brecha.

segments.src: Average them together and you get "household balance sheets are broadly healthy."
segments.tr: Promédialos juntos y obtendrás "los balances de los hogares son sanos en general".

segments.src: That statement is true of the aggregate and misleading about the distribution — which is precisely the problem with reading a $18.8 trillion figure as a single signal.
segments.tr: Esa afirmación es cierta sobre el agregado y engañosa sobre la distribución, lo que es precisamente el problema de leer una cifra de $18.8 billones como una sola señal.

segments.src: ## The part that changes the character of the debt
segments.tr: ## La parte que cambia el carácter de la deuda

segments.src: Here is the shift that matters most, and it is qualitative rather than numerical.
segments.tr: Aquí está el cambio que más importa, y es cualitativo más que numérico.

segments.src: Historically, revolving credit expanded fastest around discretionary consumption — electronics, travel, furniture, holiday spending.
segments.tr: Históricamente, el crédito revolvente se expandió más rápido en torno al consumo discrecional: electrónica, viajes, muebles, gastos navideños.

segments.src: Card debt was, broadly, a way to pull forward purchases that could otherwise have waited.
segments.tr: La deuda de tarjeta era, en términos generales, una forma de adelantar compras que de otro modo habrían esperado.

segments.src: A growing share of new non-prime borrowing now goes toward things that cannot wait.
segments.tr: Una proporción creciente del nuevo endeudamiento no prime ahora se destina a cosas que no pueden esperar.

segments.src: Surveys from the Federal Reserve, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, and multiple consumer-finance researchers have documented households using credit cards and short-term installment products for groceries, rent, utility bills, insurance premiums, and medical costs.
segments.tr: Las encuestas de la Reserva Federal, la Oficina de Protección Financiera del Consumer y múltiples investigadores de finanzas de consumo han documentado hogares que usan tarjetas de crédito y productos de pago a plazos a corto plazo para comestibles, alquiler, facturas de servicios públicos, primas de seguros y costos médicos.

segments.src: Buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) is the clearest illustration.
segments.tr: Comprar ahora, pagar después (BNPL) es la ilustración más clara.

segments.src: The product was built for mid-ticket discretionary retail — a jacket, a pair of headphones, a mattress.
segments.tr: El producto fue diseñado para el comercio minorista discrecional de precio medio: una chaqueta, un par de auriculares, un colchón.

segments.src: Its fastest-growing use cases increasingly include supermarket orders, food delivery, and everyday essentials split into four payments over six weeks.
segments.tr: Sus casos de uso de más rápido crecimiento incluyen cada vez más pedidos de supermercados, entrega de alimentos y productos esenciales cotidianos divididos en cuatro pagos durante seis semanas.

segments.src: Debt used to smooth a shortfall behaves differently from debt used to accelerate a purchase.
segments.tr: La deuda utilizada para suavizar un déficit se comporta de manera diferente a la deuda utilizada para acelerar una compra.

segments.src: A television bought on credit is a one-time obligation.
segments.tr: Un televisor comprado a crédito es una obligación única.

segments.src: Groceries bought on credit recur every week, which means the balance does not naturally retire itself — it compounds against a bill that arrives again in seven days.
segments.tr: Los comestibles comprados a crédito se repiten cada semana, lo que significa que el saldo no se retira naturalmente por sí mismo: se acumula contra una factura que llega nuevamente en siete días.

segments.src: That is why the delinquency-transition series can stay elevated even as total balances plateau: the borrowing has become less about wants and more about the gap between a paycheck and a fixed monthly cost floor.
segments.tr: Es por eso que la serie de transición de delincuencia puede mantenerse elevada incluso cuando los saldos totales se estabilizan: el endeudamiento se ha vuelto menos sobre deseos y más sobre la brecha entre un cheque de pago y un piso de costos mensuales fijos.

segments.src: ## The measurement blind spot
segments.tr: ## El punto ciego de medición

segments.src: There is an important caveat that responsible readings of this data should include: **BNPL is only partially visible.**
segments.tr: Hay una salvedad importante que las lecturas responsables de estos datos deben incluir: **BNPL solo es parcialmente visible.**

segments.src: Most BNPL "pay-in-four" plans have historically not been furnished to the traditional credit bureaus in the same consistent way as cards and installment loans.
segments.tr: La mayoría de los planes BNPL de "pago en cuatro" históricamente no se han proporcionado a las agencias de crédito tradicionales de la misma manera constante que las tarjetas y los préstamos a plazos.

segments.src: Reporting practices have been changing, and major bureaus and lenders have moved toward incorporating this data — but the transition is uneven and recent.
segments.tr: Las prácticas de informes han estado cambiando, y las principales agencias y prestamistas se han movido hacia la incorporación de estos datos, pero la transición es desigual y reciente.

segments.src: The practical consequence is that the official household-debt total almost certainly understates total consumer obligations, and that a household can appear less leveraged in bureau data than it actually is.
segments.tr: La consecuencia práctica es que el total oficial de la deuda de los hogares casi con certeza subestima las obligaciones totales de los consumidores, y que un hogar puede parecer menos apalancado en los datos de las agencias de lo que realmente está.

segments.src: It also creates "loan stacking" risk, where a borrower holds several concurrent plans from different providers, none of which can see the others.
segments.tr: También crea el riesgo de "apilamiento de préstamos", donde un prestatario tiene varios planes concurrentes de diferentes proveedores, ninguno de los cuales puede ver a los demás.

segments.src: This does not invalidate the $18.8 trillion figure.
segments.tr: Esto no invalida la cifra de $18.8 billones.

segments.src: It means the figure should be read as a floor for one category of borrowing, not a ceiling.
segments.tr: Significa que la cifra debe leerse como un piso para una categoría de endeudamiento, no como un techo.

segments.src: ## Why aggregate stability can persist for a long time
segments.tr: ## Por qué la estabilidad agregada puede persistir durante mucho tiempo

segments.src: It would be a mistake to read elevated card delinquencies as a forecast of systemic stress.
segments.tr: Sería un error leer las delinquencias de tarjetas elevadas como un pronóstico de estrés sistémico.

segments.src: Several structural factors argue against a direct 2008 analogy:
segments.tr: Varios factores estructurales argumentan en contra de una analogía directa con 2008:

segments.src: - **Mortgage debt, the dominant component, is qualitatively different this cycle.** Post-crisis underwriting standards, the near-absence of the 2000s-era exotic products, and the enormous stock of fixed-rate loans originated below 4% make the largest slice of household debt unusually resilient.
segments.tr: - **La deuda hipotecaria, el componente dominante, es cualitativamente diferente en este ciclo.** Los estándares de suscripción posteriores a la crisis, la casi ausencia de los productos exóticos de la era de 2000 y el enorme stock de préstamos a tasa fija originados por debajo del 4% hacen que la porción más grande de la deuda de los hogares sea inusualmente resistente.

segments.src: - **Credit card debt is a small share of the total.** At roughly $1.25 trillion against $18.8 trillion, cards represent under 7% of household liabilities. Severe stress in that segment is painful for the households involved and manageable for the financial system.
segments.tr: - **La deuda de tarjeta de crédito es una pequeña parte del total.** Con aproximadamente $1.25 billones frente a $18.8 billones, las tarjetas representan menos del 7% de los pasivos de los hogares. El estrés severo en ese segmento es doloroso para los hogares involucrados y manejable para el sistema financiero.

segments.src: - **Lenders have already adjusted.** Card issuers have tightened approval criteria, trimmed credit lines, and provisioned against losses over multiple quarters. The deterioration has not been a surprise to the institutions holding the exposure.
segments.tr: - **Los prestamistas ya se han ajustado.** Los emisores de tarjetas han endurecido los criterios de aprobación, recortado las líneas de crédito y provisionado contra pérdidas durante múltiples trimestres. El deterioro no ha sido una sorpresa para las instituciones que poseen la exposición.

segments.src: The realistic reading is not "crisis pending."
segments.tr: La lectura realista no es "crisis pendiente".

segments.src: It is that a meaningful and growing minority of households are running a persistent monthly deficit and financing it with the most expensive credit available to them — while the aggregate statistics, dominated by wealthier balance sheets, register that as stability.
segments.tr: Es que una minoría significativa y creciente de hogares tiene un déficit mensual persistente y lo financia con el crédito más caro disponible para ellos, mientras que las estadísticas agregadas, dominadas por balances más ricos, registran eso como estabilidad.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## Qué ver a continuación

segments.src: For anyone tracking whether the split widens or narrows, a few indicators carry more information than the headline total:
segments.tr: Para cualquier persona que rastree si la división se amplía o se estrecha, algunos indicadores contienen más información que el total principal:

segments.src: 1. **Transition-into-serious-delinquency rates by product**, especially cards and subprime auto — flows lead levels.
segments.tr: 1. **Tasas de transición a delincuencia grave por producto**, especialmente tarjetas y automóviles de alto riesgo: los flujos lideran los niveles.

segments.src: 2. **Delinquency by credit-score tier and by age cohort.** Borrowers under 40 and those in the lowest score bands have shown the sharpest deterioration.
segments.tr: 2. **Delincuencia por nivel de puntaje de crédito y por cohorte de edad.** Los prestatarios menores de 40 años y los de las bandas de puntaje más bajas han mostrado el deterioro más pronunciado.

segments.src: 3. **Revolving credit growth versus real disposable income growth.** When revolving credit outpaces income for consecutive quarters, the gap is being financed rather than closed.
segments.tr: 3. **Crecimiento del crédito revolvente frente al crecimiento del ingreso disponible real.** Cuando el crédito revolvente supera al ingreso durante trimestres consecutivos, la brecha se está financiando en lugar de cerrarse.

segments.src: 4. **BNPL reporting coverage.** As more of these plans reach the bureaus, expect reported household debt to rise for mechanical reasons. That will be a measurement artifact, not necessarily new borrowing — and it will be widely misread as one.
segments.tr: 4. **Cobertura de informes de BNPL.** A medida que más de estos planes lleguen a las agencias, espere que la deuda de los hogares reportada aumente por razones mecánicas. Eso será un artefacto de medición, no necesariamente un nuevo endeudamiento, y será malinterpretado ampliamente como uno.

segments.src: 5. **The composition of what is being financed.** Essentials-driven credit growth and discretionary-driven credit growth carry very different implications for what follows.
segments.tr: 5. **La composición de lo que se está financiando.** El crecimiento del crédito impulsado por lo esencial y el crecimiento del crédito impulsado por lo discrecional conllevan implicaciones muy diferentes para lo que sigue.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## El resultado final

segments.src: A record $18.8 trillion is not, by itself, alarming.
segments.tr: Un récord de $18.8 billones no es, por sí solo, alarmante.

segments.src: Household debt should grow with population, prices, and nominal income; records are the normal state of the series.
segments.tr: La deuda de los hogares debe crecer con la población, los precios y el ingreso nominal; los récords son el estado normal de la serie.

segments.src: What deserves attention is the divergence the total conceals: one group of households retiring debt from a position of strength, another financing groceries at revolving rates because the alternative is going without.
segments.tr: Lo que merece atención es la divergencia que el total oculta: un grupo de hogares retirando deuda desde una posición de fortaleza, otro financiando comestibles a tasas revolventes porque la alternativa es prescindir de ellos.

segments.src: Both are inside the same number.
segments.tr: Ambos están dentro del mismo número.

segments.src: Only one of them is captured by the phrase "consumer balance sheets remain solid."
segments.tr: Solo uno de ellos está capturado por la frase "los balances de los consumidores siguen sólidos".

segments.src: The averages are fine.
segments.tr: Los promedios están bien.

segments.src: The distribution is the story.
segments.tr: La distribución es la historia.
